title: tilasm: an immersive-output cycler for composing AR, XR and VR pieces as navigable stations
description:
tilasm composes immersive work as a set of stations: places a visitor stands, looks and acts. A station carries an anchor, what is seen and heard there, what the visitor can do and what answers them, the exits by which they may leave, and a comfort note stating locomotion, hazards, mitigations, floor space and what a visitor who cannot stand, cannot use both hands or cannot hear does instead.

Two checks are structural rather than stylistic. A piece in which no station leads anywhere is refused, on the grounds that an immersive work a visitor cannot move through is a picture. A station whose exit names a station that does not exist is refused as an incomplete graph. The comfort note is mandatory: a piece may legitimately require nothing, but it must say so.

Assets are brought in through the artefact inbox rather than assumed: the operator generates a model or a panorama in whichever tool they use, saves it, and selects it. Filesystem visibility is not treated as provenance.
